title: Σn Discipline
prompt:
**Scenario.** T test cases (T ≤ 1000) with per-test n; the statement guarantees Σn ≤ 200000. Your per-test algorithm is O(n^2). Which is true?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Fine: per-test n is small, so O(n^2) per test is safe

**B)** Unsafe in general: one test with n = 200000 costs 4·10^10; only the SUM is bounded

**C)** Fine because T ≤ 1000 caps everything

**D)** Unsafe only if values are large

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: Σn ≤ 200000 bounds the total, so a single test may carry all of it: per-test quadratic explodes on exactly that test. Complexity must be stated against Σn.
